name: Rustbloom Scrapper's Wrapped Street Set
description: Built around a long wrap-style top derived from a West African agbada pattern — but executed in salvaged industrial linen dyed unintentionally rust-brown by repeated acid-rain exposure, the original white fiber still visible at protected inner seams. The wrap is fixed at the shoulder with a repurposed industrial cable clamp, its chrome surface dulled by grinding but still catching light. Beneath it, a tight ribbed turtleneck in faded black synth-cotton covers the neck and wrists. The lower half is a pair of wide-leg work trousers in stiff dark brown canvas, cuffed at the ankle and belted with a length of woven nylon strap threaded through a buckle salvaged from a harness rig. Along the outer seam of each leg runs a vertical strip of reflective tape — partly for visibility in unlit tunnels, partly just because the wearer found a roll of it and it stuck. Feet are wrapped first in thick wool socks, then pushed into ankle boots resoled with layered conveyor belt rubber, the upper leather cracked to a beautiful dark-map pattern and treated with rendered fat to keep the cracks from spreading. Around the neck hangs a cord of braided copper wire strung with three salvaged BCI interface pins — non-functional, worn as jewelry — and a flat disc of oxidized steel etched by hand with a geometric pattern. Hair is wrapped in a tight cloth band cut from the same rust-brown industrial linen as the top wrap.
functionality: Turtleneck provides acid-splash protection for neck and lower face when pulled up. Wrap outer layer adds wind and rain deflection. Reflective tape strips enable visibility in unlit industrial zones. Resoled boots handle broken grating and chemical puddles. Cargo capacity in trouser pockets. Copper wire neck cord doubles as basic conductive tool for scavenging electronics.
what_it_says: There's aesthetic intent here — the wrap construction, the hand-etched steel disc, the BCI pins worn as ornament rather than function. This person is not just surviving; they're maintaining a sense of self within the survival. The Shelf has style, and this outfit insists on it quietly.
worn_by: younger Shelf residents with a sense of identity
people who grew up poor but grew up with taste
manufacturer: Self-constructed; linen sourced from Drift Market salvage stalls
story_hooks: The three BCI interface pins worn as jewelry are recognized by a black-market tech runner as components from a prototype neural array — suddenly the wearer's scrap jewelry is worth more than everything else they own combined.
The hand-etched geometric pattern on the steel disc is a Shelf gang territorial mark — wearing it in the wrong tunnel section draws immediate, aggressive attention.

A TESSERA Genomics field researcher on a covert survey notices the acid-dye pattern on the linen wrap matches a specific industrial runoff signature from a facility that was supposed to be decommissioned — the wearer's clothes are environmental evidence.

physical_description.visual_profile: A striking silhouette that blends West African textile tradition with industrial salvage aesthetics. The long wrap-top drapes generously from one shoulder, creating asymmetrical volume and movement. The figure appears grounded and deliberate — neither wealthy nor desperate, but resourceful. The overall impression is of someone who has crafted identity from necessity, where every element tells a story of reclamation.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately relaxed and layered. The wrap-top is loose and flowing, anchored at one shoulder by the cable clamp. The turtleneck underneath is compression-fit, creating contrast between the two layers. The trousers are wide-leg and substantial, sitting at the natural waist with a generous break at the ankle.
physical_description.primary_material: Salvaged industrial linen (rust-brown, acid-rain weathered), faded black synth-cotton turtleneck, stiff dark brown canvas work trousers, cracked leather ankle boots, conveyor belt rubber resoling, braided copper wire jewelry
physical_description.texture: Rough and lived-in. The linen is stiff yet broken in, with visible fiber degradation at stress points. Canvas has a dense weave with creasing at flex points. Leather upper is deeply cracked into a map-like pattern. Rubber sole is layered and industrial. Copper wire has natural patina and corrosion marks.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant rust-brown (acid-rain oxidation), deep charcoal black, dark chocolate brown canvas, oxidized copper accents, dulled chrome from cable clamp, reflective silver-gray tape, pale cream linen at hidden seams, weathered leather browns and blacks
physical_description.closures: Industrial cable clamp at shoulder (fixed, non-adjustable), nylon strap belt with salvaged harness buckle at waist, lace-up boots with worn leather ties
distinctive_features: Repurposed industrial cable clamp as functional shoulder anchor
Visible white fiber at protected inner seams contrasting rust exterior
Vertical reflective tape strips down outer leg seams
Hand-etched steel disc pendant on braided copper wire collar
Three non-functional salvaged BCI interface pins strung on neck cord
Hair wrapped in matching rust-brown linen band
Conveyor belt rubber layered boot resoling
Leather boots with natural cracking pattern resembling geographic maps
Fat-treated boot leather to preserve integrity
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 sub-grade/ungoverned. This is not poverty — it is deliberate anti-consumerism and resourcefulness. The wearer has rejected corpo fashion entirely in favor of salvage-assembled identity.
physical_description.cultural_context: Scrapper, tunnel worker, or Drift Market dweller. The West African agbada pattern suggests cultural memory or heritage knowledge. The BCI pins and copper wire suggest technical interest without corporate augmentation. The reflective tape and work trousers indicate someone who navigates dark industrial spaces. This is someone who has learned to see beauty in rust and wear.
physical_description.condition_typical: Thoroughly broken-in and weathered. Every element shows honest use — creases in the canvas follow the body's motion, the leather map-cracks deepen with wear, dust settles into seams, the reflective tape corners lift slightly. Not pristine, not destroyed — maintained with intention and rendered fat.
